narrative.overview:
The whole application is one continuous seyès-ruled page — the ruled sheet every French lycee student writes their homework on — not a dashboard of cards floating on a page-shaped background. A student opens it several times a day to decide what to do next and what to revise, and it earns trust by looking like the cahier they already keep: bright Clairefontaine-white ground, a bold school-ink-blue rule down the left margin, faint blue-violet ruling behind the content, and every line of type set down onto the baseline.

The 8mm carreau is the single layout unit. --carreau is 1.75rem (28px); it is simultaneously the ruling pitch, the body line-height, and the module every gap, padding and measure is a multiple of. The left margin rule sits at four carreaux from the edge (--marge, halved to two on mobile). Colour follows strict Bic four-colour semantics and never decorates: ink-blue is structure, links, and the margin; graphite is body text; Bic red is to-do / important / a teacher's mark / an error; Bic green is done. State is drawn into the page — a green pen-stroke check in the margin, a single strike-through, a red grade written large in the margin on the Notes page — rather than floated above it. Navigation is a row of classeur intercalaire tabs with the active tab joined to the page.

The system explicitly refuses the sidebar-plus-card-grid ed-tech dashboard, resting shadows, card borders over 1px, coloured left-stripe accents, and any glyph or emoji iconography (icons are an authored hand-inked SVG set, one ~1.6 stroke weight, round caps). Dark mode is the same page at night under a desk lamp: deep ink-blue ground (--paper #151b2e), luminous ruling, warm off-white ink; it is class-driven (.dark), user-toggled, and persisted.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous ruled page; no floating card grid.
The 8mm carreau (1.75rem) is the only layout unit — every measure is a multiple of it.
Bold ink-blue margin rule at 4 carreaux left; faint blue-violet ruling behind content.
Strict Bic four-colour semantics; colour is never decorative.
Square corners (2px), 1px lines only, no resting shadows.
Spectral serif for titles, Atkinson Hyperlegible for body, Fragment Mono for figures — all set on the carreau baseline.
State is drawn into the page: margin tick, struck line, red teacher's mark.
Dark mode is a first-class night version of the same page, .dark-driven and persisted.

rules.name: The Bic Four-Colour Rule
rules.body: Ink-blue = structure / links / margin. Graphite = body. Bic red = to-do / important / teacher's mark / error. Bic green = done. A new surface uses exactly these four roles; introducing a fifth hue is off-system. Subject colours from Scolengo are the one sanctioned exception and appear only as a 1px full border plus a ~12% tinted fill plus coloured caps — never a stripe.

rules.name: The Colour Is Never Decorative Rule
rules.body: If a colour on screen is not carrying one of the four semantic roles, it is a bug. Test: name the role of every non-graphite mark on the page. No answer means remove it.

rules.name: The Baseline Rule
rules.body: Body text is leaded to exactly var(--carreau) (line-height: var(--carreau)) so every line lands on the ruling. New text blocks inherit the carreau leading; never set an arbitrary line-height on reading copy.

rules.name: The Figures Are Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything that is data — a time, a grade, a date, a count — is set in Fragment Mono with .tabulaire so columns align. Prose is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Carreau Rule
rules.body: --carreau (1.75rem / 28px) is the only layout unit. Every gap, padding, height, offset and max-width is a multiple or simple fraction of it (calc(var(--carreau)*n)). A raw px or rem value that is not a carreau multiple is off-system.

rules.name: The Margin Rule
rules.body: Every screen carries the ink-blue margin rule down the left at four carreaux (two on mobile). Primary actions and the date/marker gutter live in the space to its left; body content starts one carreau to its right.

rules.name: The No Resting Shadow Rule
rules.body: A resting surface has no shadow — ever. A shadow means 'this slip is floating above the page' (dropdown, modal). It is a warm near-black offset (down and right, like a lamp), never a symmetric ambient glow.

rules.name: The 1px Line Rule
rules.body: Every border and divider is 1px. No coloured left-stripe accents anywhere — a subject or status is shown by a full box, a tinted fill, coloured caps, or a mark in the margin.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is 2px everywhere via the rounded-sm token. Don't introduce a new radius; the only round things are the pen check and the letter marks.

dos: Do size every measure as a carreau multiple — var(--carreau), calc(var(--carreau)*n), or the carreau spacing token (The Carreau Rule).
Do carry the ink-blue margin rule on every screen and keep the primary action / marker in the gutter left of it (The Margin Rule).
Do lead body text to var(--carreau) so it sits on the ruling (The Baseline Rule).
Do keep colour strictly semantic: ink-blue structure, graphite body, Bic red to-do/important/mark/error, Bic green done (The Bic Four-Colour Rule).
Do draw state into the page — a margin check, a strike-through, a red grade in the margin — not onto a floated badge.
Do set all times, dates, grades and counts in Fragment Mono with .tabulaire.
Do use .regle for lined pages and .carreaux for the timetable and calendar.
Do ship every surface in both themes via the .dark class, with a real night value for every colour used.
Do use the authored Icone set at 1.6 stroke weight for every icon.
donts: Don't build a sidebar-plus-card-grid dashboard; the app is one continuous page.
Don't put a shadow on a resting surface — a shadow means a slip is floating (The No Resting Shadow Rule).
Don't use a border over 1px, or any coloured left-stripe accent; show a subject or status as a full box, tint, caps or margin mark (The 1px Line Rule).
Don't introduce a new radius; corners are 2px via rounded-sm (The Square Corner Rule).
Don't introduce a fifth hue or use any colour decoratively (The Colour Is Never Decorative Rule).
Don't use emoji, unicode symbols, or an icon font.
Don't set reading copy in Fragment Mono or at an arbitrary line-height.
Don't rely on colour alone for a state — pair it with the check mark, the strike, or a letter mark.
